extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, OED/USPTO staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for imposing reciprocal discipline (public reprimand) by the USPTO based on a state disciplinary sanction, and the respondent's opportunity and obligations to contest such reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(6) — public reprimand by state authority
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may be disciplined under USPTO rules for having been publicly reprimanded on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State (constituting a violation of 37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: In The Florida Bar v. Richard Allen Buckley (Case No. SC08-521), the Florida Supreme Court approved a settlement publicly reprimanding the practitioner for drafting and recording an Affidavit and Notice of Interest in Real Estate that was frivolous, without legal basis, and/or designed to exert unjustifiable pressure by precluding sale of property. The practitioner admitted violating Rules Regulating the Florida Bar 4-8.4(d) (conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice) and agreed to public reprimand. Such a state public reprimand is the factual/legal basis for USPTO reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's burden to contest reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director requests reciprocal discipline, the respondent may contest imposition of identical discipline by filing a response within 40 days that contains all information the respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The response must specifically identify facts or legal grounds under §11.24(d)(1) that would make imposition of identical discipline unwarranted. Failure to file a timely response (or failure to show a genuine issue of material fact) results in a determination that no genuine issue exists and the identical discipline will be imposed. (Here, respondent did not file a response, and the Office determined there was no genuine issue and ordered a public reprimand.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement for final order (37 C.F.R. §11.24 and §11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order imposing discipline and shall publish a notice of reprimand in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order must be made public and the Official Gazette notice should summarize the discipline, identify the respondent and registration number, and state the violation(s) and the originating state disciplinary action. The Final Order may also be posted in the OED Reading Room (URL provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public (37 C.F.R. §11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 37 C.F.R. §11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice requirement ensures other jurisdictions and the public are informed of USPTO action; the Final Order instructs OED to carry out these notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of Official Gazette 'Notice of Reprimand'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Gazette notice must identify the practitioner (name and registration number), state that a public reprimand was ordered, summarize the underlying state disciplinary proceeding and the conduct found, cite the state case and the state rule(s) violated, and state the statutory/regulatory authority for the USPTO action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision includes an exemplar notice that names the respondent, cites the Florida case, summarizes the allegation (drafting/recording frivolous affidavit/notice of interest intended to exert unjustifiable pressure), cites the Florida Bar rule violated (4-8.4(d)), and cites U.S. statutory and regulatory authority (35 U.S.C. §§2(b)(2)(D) and 32; 37 C.F.R. §§11.24 and 11.59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory basis for USPTO disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO disciplinary actions under this Final Order are taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing these provisions establishes the USPTO's authority to impose reciprocal discipline and to publish/notify regarding disciplinary actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and mailing requirements (certificate of service; 37 C.F.R. §11.11 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Orders and related documents must be mailed to the respondent by first class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the most recent address provided to OED pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.11 and to any address at which OED believes the respondent receives mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision includes a Certificate of Service showing mailing to the addresses provided and to other addresses believed to be effective; proper service is a procedural prerequisite to finalizing notice.
